claims.claim: Brought news New York (yesterday) news to 1866-06-24
claims.citation: New York Herald, 3 July 1866, p. 6, col. 1
claims.verbatim:
By the arrival yesterday of the steamships Bremen,
Bavaria, City of Boston and Merrimac, at this port, and
Cuba, at Halifax, we received news from Europe, by
mail and telegraph, to the 24th of June, seven days later.

claims.citation: New York Herald, 2 July 1866, p. 4, col. 1
claims.verbatim:
The European news, dated to the 21st of June, so anx-
iously expected yesterday, had not arrived when the
HERALD went to press this morning. The steamships
Bavaria, Bremen, City of Boston and Damascus are due
at this port and off Father Point respectively.

claims.citation: New York Herald, 4 July 1866, p. 2, col. 5
claims.verbatim:
Our European[?] files, dated to the 20th of June, al-
though not so late as the telegraphic report of the Cuba,
contain some very interesting details of the news to the
time of the sailing of the City of Boston.

claims.citation: New York Herald, 3 July 1866, p. 9, col. 1
claims.verbatim: under the advices by the City of Boston, which were one day later than those by the Bremen, and which reported an advance in American securities on the London Stock Exchange.
